title: Hilton London Hyde Park: Hitchcock's Frenzy Hotel
description: Hilton London Hyde Park, once the Coburg Hotel, appears in Hitchcock's Frenzy. Film facts and history of this Bayswater hotel in London.
h1: Hilton London Hyde Park: the Coburg Hotel from Hitchcock's Frenzy
intro: Overlooking Hyde Park on Bayswater Road, this hotel was known as the Coburg when Alfred Hitchcock came to film there. Its brief but memorable appearance is in his 1972 thriller Frenzy.
filming: In Frenzy, the fugitive Richard Blaney takes Babs Milligan to the Coburg, where they sign in as Mr. and Mrs. Oscar Wilde. Filming took place at the hotel in September 1971, though most of the interiors were recreated at Pinewood Studios. The shot of the police looking at the fire escape was filmed from a fifth-floor room.
facts: The hotel opened in 1907 as the Coburg Court Hotel.
It was renamed the Coburg Hotel in the early 1960s.
It has carried the Hilton name since July 1999.
The hotel has 136 rooms and looks out over Hyde Park and Kensington Gardens.
visit: The hotel is next to Queensway station, with Hyde Park across the road. Check the booking page for current rates and availability.
